accepted.s: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched at which place and event?
o: Gwal Pahari during the laying of the headquarters foundation stone
New Delhi during the founding conference of ISA
accepted.x: The ISA was launched jointly by India and France on 30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris.
accepted.tq: Use the event-location pair to distinguish the launch from later ISA milestones.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance:
1. It is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation.
2. Its headquarters is located at Gurugram in Haryana.
3. Its secretariat is located at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The ISA is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation headquartered at Gurugram, Haryana. Its secretariat is also associated with Gurugram, not New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the organisation’s legal status and location separately.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: The foundation stone of the International Solar Alliance headquarters was laid at which location?
accepted.x: The foundation stone was laid at the National Institute of Solar Energy campus at Gwal Pahari, Gurugram, on 25 January 2016.
accepted.tq: Test the precise location rather than the broader city or country.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: Who laid the foundation stone of the International Solar Alliance headquarters?
o: The Prime Ministers of India and France
The President of France and the Director-General of ISA
accepted.x: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and French President François Hollande laid the foundation stone at Gwal Pahari, Gurugram.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish the founding leaders.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: The Framework Agreement of the International Solar Alliance entered into force on:
accepted.x: The ISA Framework Agreement entered into force on 6 December 2017, giving the organisation its treaty-based character.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the agreement’s effective date from the launch and foundation-stone dates.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: The founding conference of the International Solar Alliance was held on:
accepted.x: The founding conference of the ISA was held on 11 March 2018 in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Use date-place pairing to separate the founding conference from other milestones.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change in membership eligibility of the International Solar Alliance?
o: Membership was initially for Sunshine Countries and was later opened to all UN members through a 2020 amendment.
Membership is available only to countries that have installed more than 1 GW of solar capacity.
Membership continues to be restricted exclusively to countries between the tropics.
Membership was initially restricted to European countries and later opened to Asian countries.
accepted.x: The ISA initially focused on Sunshine Countries located between the tropics. A 2020 amendment opened membership to all United Nations members.
accepted.tq: Track the change from the original restricted membership to the amended broader rule.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: Romania is associated with which of the following developments concerning the International Solar Alliance?
o: It laid the foundation stone of the ISA headquarters.
It hosted the launch of ISA at COP21.
It ratified the ISA Framework Agreement in 2026.
accepted.x: Romania ratified the International Solar Alliance Framework Agreement in 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the country with the specific institutional action rather than the launch event.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: OSOWOG — Pooling demand for bulk procurement of solar equipment
Common procurement platform — Pooling demand to reduce costs through scale
ISA Academy — Treaty-making body of the ISA
accepted.x: The common procurement platform pools demand so that costs can be reduced through economies of scale. OSOWOG concerns an interconnected solar grid, while STAR-C concerns training and best practices.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure functional pair and eliminate swapped purposes.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about ISA initiatives:
1. OSOWOG seeks to facilitate the sharing of solar power across borders and time zones.
2. STAR-C functions as a platform for knowledge, training and best practices.
3. The common procurement platform is intended to reduce costs through pooled demand.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the purposes of OSOWOG, STAR-C and the common procurement platform.
accepted.tq: Check each initiative against its distinct function before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: Which of the following initiatives was launched at the 8th Assembly of the International Solar Alliance held in New Delhi?
accepted.x: The Global SIDS Initiative, ISA Academy, Global Capability Centre and SUNRISE were launched at the 8th ISA Assembly in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Find the initiative belonging to the ISA rather than a domestic solar programme.
accepted.sec: International Solar Alliance - HQ, founding, members, initiatives

accepted.s: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission is popularly known by which brand name?
accepted.x: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission was launched under the brand name “Solar India”.
accepted.tq: Test the official brand-name association directly.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission is one of the missions under which framework?
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change
accepted.x: The National Solar Mission is one of the eight missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change, adopted in 2008.
accepted.tq: Identify the parent policy framework rather than the implementing ministry or programme.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: The original target of the National Solar Mission for grid-connected solar capacity by 2022 was:
accepted.x: The original target was 20 GW of grid-connected solar capacity by 2022. It was revised in June 2015 to 100 GW.
accepted.tq: Separate the original target from the subsequently revised target.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: In June 2015, the grid-connected solar target under the National Solar Mission was revised to:
accepted.x: The target was revised in June 2015 from 20 GW to 100 GW by 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the revision date and target as a paired numerical fact.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: The revised target of 100 GW under the National Solar Mission comprised:
o: 60 GW rooftop and 40 GW off-grid solar
20 GW rooftop and 80 GW large-scale solar
40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large/medium grid-connected solar
50 GW rooftop and 50 GW solar parks
accepted.x: The revised 100 GW target consisted of 40 GW from rooftop solar and 60 GW from large and medium grid-connected projects.
accepted.tq: Break the aggregate target into its two component shares.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Phase)
a. Phase I
b. Phase II
c. Phase III

List-II (Period)
i. 2017–2022
ii. 2010–2013
iii. 2014–2017

Codes:
accepted.x: Phase I covered 2010–2013, Phase II covered 2014–2017, and Phase III covered 2017–2022.
accepted.tq: Start with the first phase and eliminate codes with a misplaced period.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the off-grid solar photovoltaic targets of the three phases of the National Solar Mission?
accepted.x: The off-grid solar PV targets were 200 MW in Phase I, 1,000 MW in Phase II and 2,000 MW in Phase III.
accepted.tq: Read the sequence across the phases without reversing the progression.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding other targets of the National Solar Mission:
1. Solar thermal collector area was targeted at 15 million square metres by 2017.
2. Solar thermal collector area was targeted at 20 million square metres by 2022.
3. Twenty million solar lighting systems were targeted for rural areas by 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Mission included targets of 15 million square metres of solar thermal collectors by 2017, 20 million square metres by 2022 and 20 million rural solar lighting systems by 2022.
accepted.tq: Check the years and units carefully before accepting the combined option.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a policy instrument associated with the National Solar Mission?
o: Compulsory replacement of all coal plants by nuclear plants
accepted.x: Renewable Purchase Obligations, preferential tariffs, solar parks and research and development were associated with the Mission. Compulsory replacement of coal plants by nuclear plants was not one of its stated instruments.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated policy toolkit rather than focusing only on the familiar terms.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: The successor long-term goal associated with India’s solar-energy transition is:
accepted.x: India’s successor goal is 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, associated with its COP26 pledge.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the broader non-fossil target from the earlier solar-only target.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases

accepted.s: India’s non-fossil electricity capacity had reached what share by December 2025, according to the stated assessment?
accepted.x: The non-fossil capacity share was reported as 51.93% by December 2025, exceeding the 50% milestone ahead of schedule.
accepted.tq: Use the precise percentage rather than the nearby rounded milestone.
accepted.sec: National Solar Mission - launch, targets, phases
